title: Marvell to Buy Lumentum in $115 Billion All-Stock Bet on AI Optical Connectivity
excerpt: Lumentum holders get a fixed 4.500 Marvell shares per share, a 23.9% premium, in a deal the companies say creates a category leader for AI data-center connectivity, with closing expected in the first half of 2028.
body:
• Marvell Technology will acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion, the companies announced on Monday, November 2.
  • Lumentum shareholders will receive a fixed 4.500 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share, worth about $1,132 per share at October 28 prices, a premium of about 23.9%.
  • The deal pairs Marvell's custom silicon and switching with Lumentum's lasers and optical transceivers as AI data centers shift from copper to optical links.
  • Closing is expected in the first half of 2028, subject to shareholder votes at both companies and regulatory approvals.

Marvell Technology has agreed to acquire optical components maker Lumentum in an all-stock transaction that values Lumentum at an implied enterprise value of $115 billion, the two companies announced on Monday. It is among the largest semiconductor deals ever announced, and it is a direct bet on how AI data centers will be wired: with light, not copper.

Under the definitive agreement, Lumentum stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.500 shares of Marvell common stock for each Lumentum share they own. Based on closing prices on October 28, 2026, the last trading day before market speculation about a deal began, that works out to about $1,132 per Lumentum share, a premium of about 23.9%. After closing, Marvell stockholders will own about 67% of the combined company and Lumentum stockholders about 33%, on a fully diluted basis. Because the exchange ratio is fixed, the final dollar value of the deal will move with Marvell's share price until it closes.

"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation."

— Matt Murphy, Chairman and CEO, Marvell

Why optical, and why now

The companies argue that rapidly growing bandwidth requirements, and the physical limits of copper-based connectivity, are pushing AI clusters toward optical technology, especially as architectures scale up within racks and scale in within packages. Marvell brings electrical and optical interconnect, network switching, custom processors and advanced packaging. Lumentum brings high-performance lasers, optical transceivers, optical circuit switching and specialized compound semiconductor manufacturing, including indium phosphide. The combined company says it will be able to co-design across the full electrical and optical signal chain, from connections between distributed data centers down to links inside advanced semiconductor packages.

https://x.com/garyblack00/status/2117276050333831442

Lumentum President and CEO Michael Hurlston said joining Marvell positions the combined company for what the companies estimate is a $550 billion market opportunity. That figure is the companies' own estimate. The companies also project more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies and expect the deal to add to Marvell's non-GAAP earnings per share in the first year after closing. Both figures are company projections, not results.

Terms, leadership and timeline

Both boards approved the agreement unanimously. Matt Murphy will continue as chairman and CEO of the combined company, and three Lumentum directors, including Hurlston, will join Marvell's board, which currently has seven members. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of calendar 2028, subject to approval by both companies' stockholders, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions, according to the joint announcement.

Alongside the deal, Marvell reported preliminary fiscal third-quarter 2027 revenue consistent with its earlier guidance, narrowing its expected range to plus or minus 2%. Lumentum separately reported its fiscal first-quarter 2027 results the same day. A shareholder-law firm, Ademi LLP, has already announced an investigation into whether the buyout fairly values Lumentum, a routine step after large US deals that can precede litigation over price.

What to watch

Two things will decide whether this deal delivers: regulators, and integration. A combination of this size in AI infrastructure components will draw antitrust scrutiny in the US and abroad, and the 2028 closing target leaves a long window in which Marvell's share price, and therefore the deal's value to Lumentum holders, can move substantially. For investors in either stock, the fixed 4.500 exchange ratio, not the $115 billion headline, is the number that governs what they will actually own.
